note: The snapshot a pass restores the build tree from (register decisions 506 and 512-519). Each mutant takes away one part of the put-back -- the outputs, what the tests wrote, the second listing, the source's time, the check of git's bytes, the build's check, the second restore after it -- or one of the rules around it: a leftover snapshot, --restore, and the main loop putting the tree back after each mutant. All are judged by mutate.py's self-test, which runs the put-back on a tree of plain files and on a scratch project CMake configures and Ninja builds, and a whole two-mutant pass shaped as m1-95.json is. Two survive, declared: the order of the put-back's steps, and the check of the snapshot's copies. Since item 7 (register decisions 520-524) also Ninja's stored answers and their key, the fingerprints check's fresh reading, a judge the tree does not have -- run by ctest, at the start of a pass, in --verify and in the due-list -- a file with no mutants, and a mutant file's own mutants as its input: judged by mutants-due.py's self-test, mutate.py's, and the CTest test mutants_due_mutant_file.
